name: Eurasianism
summary: Eurasianism holds that Russia and its neighbouring lands form a distinct civilisation between Europe and Asia, to be united in a Eurasian state or union and set against Western, liberal universalism. Classical Eurasianists of the 1920s favoured an authoritarian, Orthodox-inflected ideocratic state and a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis, while neo-Eurasianism adds geopolitical opposition to the Atlantic bloc, a strong state and traditionalism.
scope: Classical Eurasianism of Trubetskoy, Savitsky, Florovsky and Alekseev, together with the neo-Eurasianism of Aleksandr Dugin, which is the version in current use. Where they differ, answers follow what both share (anti-West, empire, civilisational unity, strong state, religion). Economic and many social answers are inferred with low confidence.

office-by-exam.rationale: Classical Eurasianists proposed an ideocratic state led by a selected ruling stratum rather than by popular election; inferred.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism opposes Atlantic economic penetration and favours a state-directed strong economy, so blocking foreign takeovers is inferred as agreed.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: The Orthodox-inflected, traditionalist outlook tells against easy divorce; inferred.

recallable-delegates.rationale: Eurasianists favoured an authoritarian, ideocratic state and criticised Western liberal democracy, so instructed and recallable delegates is inferred as opposed.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: The state-directed, strong-state economic outlook favours state-run provision over private accounts; inferred.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Eurasianists did not set a land tenure doctrine; a state-guided economy and private holdings both fit, so inferred as split.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Eurasianism prefers a strong, ideocratic executive over a liberal parliament, so parliamentary budget approval as a condition is inferred as disfavoured.

single-official-language.rationale: Eurasianism praises a multi-ethnic Slavic-Turkic union, so restricting other languages for one sole language is inferred as disfavoured.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism treats national land as sovereign civilisational territory against Atlantic influence; inferred.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Dugin rejects Western universalist liberal norms, which include outcome-based anti-discrimination; inferred.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Eurasianism sets traditional and spiritual values against Western materialist consumer culture; inferred.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: The Foundations of Geopolitics advocates destabilising Atlanticist states and supporting separatist and opposition movements; inferred as agreed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Eurasianism sees a Russia-led Eurasian bloc and its empire as a unity to be held together, so intervention to keep members in the bloc is inferred as agreed.

corporate-influence.rationale: Opposes Western liberal markets in favour of a state-directed economy; influence of private corporations is inferred as unwelcome.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Central opposition to Western influence and Atlanticism implies restricting foreign-funded NGOs, media and universities in the Eurasian space.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: Traditionalism and a strong civilisational state imply support for family and birth-rate policy; inferred.

residents-only-property.rationale: Sovereignty and rootedness in place are stressed; limiting property to locals is inferred rather than stated.

job-guarantee.rationale: A statist third-way economy under a strong state implies state responsibility for employment; inferred.

democratic-peace.rationale: Rejects liberal universalism and Western democracy promotion as a form of Atlantic hegemony.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Favours an authoritarian ideocratic state with obedience to the national idea; inferred.

non-intervention.rationale: Opposes Western intervention but claims a Russian sphere of influence over neighbouring lands, so a universal ban is not held.

industrial-unions.rationale: Economic organisation of labour was not a focus; no stance can be inferred.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Classical Eurasianism stressed Slavic-Turkic symbiosis and a multi-ethnic civilisation; Atlanticist conspiracy talk is not aimed at a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Traditionalism and Orthodox-inflected values imply keeping marriage as a legal institution; inferred.

public-access-to-information.rationale: An authoritarian ideocratic state is unlikely to endorse a legal right to government information; inferred.

local-production.rationale: Opposes globalisation and favours autarky of large economic spaces, though not strictly local production; inferred.

informal-organisation.rationale: The ideocratic state is led by an organised elite and movement, opposite to informal leaderless groups; inferred.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Rejects Western-dominated international law and universal human-rights norms in favour of civilisational sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: Orthodoxy has a central role in the Russian national state, but Eurasia is conceived as multi-confessional, so the answer is mixed.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Not directly addressed; Eurasianists want a Russian-led union but insist on equality of civilisations, so adherents are split on ritual deference.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Inferred from the call for a strong centralised Eurasian state rather than regional autonomy over revenue.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Not addressed; Dugin's third-way economy leaves the personal/productive line unspecified.

defeat-communism.rationale: Inferred: neo-Eurasianism is hostile to liberal capitalism more than to Soviet-style statism, and Dugin has National Bolshevik sympathies.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a statist but non-doctrinaire third-way economy.

religion-illusion.rationale: Orthodoxy and traditional religion are central to Eurasianism, which holds that religion is a lasting foundation of civilisation.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Eurasianists reject Western liberal modernity and its market society as a model for Russia and the world.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's traditionalist stress on family and gender roles.

socialized-care.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist emphasis on the family as a basic unit.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; adherents have no clear doctrine on language purism.

treaties-binding.rationale: Inferred from the imperial, centralising model under which the state ultimately decides.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Inferred: the model is a unified Eurasian state or empire, not many small communes.

majority-settlement.rationale: Classical Eurasianists favoured a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis, but the neo-Eurasian empire involves Russian leadership; adherents split.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Dugin's Fourth Political Theory rejects liberalism, communism and fascism alike and Eurasianism claims a distinct third path.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Eurasianism rests on the idea of a Eurasian space bound to its peoples by history, and neo-Eurasianism uses it to justify claims over neighbouring lands.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Not part of the doctrine; inferred rejection, though some in the wider milieu flirt with revisionism.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Dugin's traditionalism is hostile to homosexuality and sympathetic to criminal or legal bans; inferred from his traditionalism, with classical Eurasianists silent.

suppress-opposition.rationale: Classical Eurasianists favoured an authoritarian single-ideology (ideocratic) state, and neo-Eurasianism a strong state.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: The ideocratic state was Orthodox-inflected and Eurasianists gave the Church a national role, so legal protection of the faith follows.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Eurasianists present empire as a symbiosis of peoples rather than exploitation, though they back imperial rule; inferred.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: A specifically Islamic obligation; Eurasianism treats Islam as a partner but takes no position on this.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: They favour religiously grounded states but no source endorses removing rulers by force over religious law; inferred.

participatory-democracy.rationale: They denounce liberal democracy while Dugin uses participatory language for a corporate and ethnic order, so adherents are split; inferred.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is militantly opposed to Western progressive identity politics; inferred from its anti-liberalism.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Dugin's traditionalism rejects Western gender liberalisation; inferred.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Orthodox-inflected traditionalism.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Eurasianism presents itself as a third position beyond liberalism, communism and fascism, combining elements of right and left.

alienated-labor.rationale: Anti-capitalist but not in Marxian terms; the idea was not addressed and adherents would be split.

islam-incompatible.rationale: Eurasianism builds on a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis and treats Islam as part of Eurasian civilisation, not as alien to it.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: The classical ideocratic state drew on Orthodox religion and Eurasianists stress the Church's role in the national state.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: They favour a role for religion in public life, so bans on religious dress are inferred to be disfavoured.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: A modern employment-law matter outside the doctrine; no position inferable.

social-market-economy.rationale: Economic views are a vague statist third way between liberal capitalism and socialism, so adherents are split on this specific model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is built on great-power geopolitics and military strength against the Atlantic bloc.

rich-first.rationale: Not addressed; state-directed economic views leave adherents split.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Eurasianism is itself a rival bloc strategy, with Russia leading a Eurasian union against the Atlantic bloc.

dynastic-succession.rationale: Inferred from the classical ideocratic state ruled by a selected elite rather than a dynasty; not discussed directly.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Not addressed; neo-Eurasianism favours a state-directed third-way economy without a stated view on cooperative credit.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: Inferred from the opposition to Western liberal institutions and the Atlantic bloc, though lenders as such were not addressed.

property-franchise.rationale: Inferred from the ideocratic selection of a ruling elite by commitment to the idea, not property; not stated.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is traditionalist and rejects Western feminist and liberal ecological frames; inferred.

reification.rationale: Dugin criticises liberal commodification but this Marxist concept is not part of Eurasianist doctrine.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Inferred from the view that Western liberal freedoms mask the control of money and the Atlantic bloc over the media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian ideocratic strong state that rules by the national idea rather than liberal legal limits.

racial-franchise.rationale: Eurasianism is explicitly multi-ethnic, stressing the Slavic-Turkic symbiosis and rejecting Romano-Germanic chauvinism, so a single-group franchise is not its position.

online-participation.rationale: Not addressed; the strong-state and traditionalist outlook leaves adherents without a clear view.

open-government-data.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, ideocratic strong state, which does not favour open records.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox, Muslim and Buddhist cooperation in the Eurasian civilisation; marriage law was not addressed.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: Inferred from the multi-confessional and multi-ethnic civilisational unity it promotes.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Classical Eurasianists favoured an authoritarian ideocratic state and Dugin a strong hierarchical one, so decision by randomly chosen citizens runs against it; inferred, not addressed directly.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Eurasianists stress Orthodoxy and traditionalism as civilisational foundations and reject Western modernising reform of the faith; inferred from that emphasis.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the statist third-way economy that opposes liberal oligarchic capital.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is traditionalist and Orthodox-inflected and Dugin attacks Western liberal social norms, so open gay military service is rejected.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Eurasianists hold that Orthodoxy and religion belong at the centre of the national state, so state atheism is opposed.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Eurasianism favours an authoritarian strong state, so abolishing police and prisons is opposed.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Inferred from the ideocratic, centralised strong-state model and rejection of liberal Western institutions, which cuts against formal power sharing.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Not addressed; Orthodox communal solidarity is valued but the strong state also directs welfare.

term-limits.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, leader-centred ideal of the state; term limits on rulers are not in the programme.

vote-delegation.rationale: Inferred from rejection of Western liberal democracy and the preference for an authoritarian ideocratic state.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Not addressed; the ideology is geopolitical and civilisational, with no stated position on extinction risk.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is aligned with Orthodox and traditionalist religion, which restricts religious office to men, and Dugin defends traditional gender roles.

shared-marital-authority.rationale: Dugin's traditionalism defends patriarchal family order against Western liberal gender equality.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the civilisational-unity and strong-state outlook, which gives citizenship a thick cultural meaning.

rent-control.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the state-directed, socially minded economy the neo-Eurasians favour.

abolish-ip.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a state-directed economy that has no quarrel with intellectual property.

uniformed-youth.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the ideocratic, Orthodox-inflected state that mobilises society for a common mission.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Not addressed directly; inferred from geopolitics that treats Russian strategic power, including its deterrent, as the core of Eurasian independence.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Opposition to the Atlantic bloc and US military presence in Eurasia is central to Dugin's geopolitics.

recognise-genocide.rationale: Not addressed; inferred, since a state-centred imperial outlook may use or reject genocide recognition depending on whose history is at stake.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the anti-liberal, socially oriented third-way economy.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from an imperial, geopolitical-struggle outlook that has no pacifist strand.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: Inferred from the claim that Russia-Eurasia is a continuous civilisation inheriting earlier steppe and Orthodox empires.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditionalism that treats sex differences as given.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from traditionalist opposition to Western liberal gender theory.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Inferred from the Orthodox-inflected state ideology, in which dying for the homeland carries sacred meaning.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: Dugin frames geopolitics as a metaphysical clash between sacred tradition and Western liberal modernity, and the classical Eurasianists wanted an ideocratic state.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Inferred from the view of Russia as the centre of a wider Eurasian civilisation that includes peoples outside it.

culture-before-state.rationale: Trubetskoy stresses cultural distinctness, but Eurasianists also demand a strong state, so the order is not settled.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the Orthodox tradition the Eurasianists defend.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the defence of Orthodox tradition against Western liberal critique.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: Eurasianism is a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis in one empire, so it neither favours the Russian majority alone nor treats minorities equally in the economy.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Inferred from a multi-ethnic empire model that unites peoples in one state rather than carving out a unit for each.

independent-unions.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strong, ideocratic state and corporate unity that Eurasianists favour over autonomous civil society.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: Eurasianism sets civilisational and state unity above class politics, and Dugin rejects Marxism, so workers' own power is not the test of legitimacy.

local-essentials-public.rationale: Inferred from the preference for a strong, state-directed economy; local services are not discussed.

second-chamber.rationale: Not addressed; classical Eurasianists proposed an ideocratic selected elite and neo-Eurasianists a strong executive, so no clear stance on chambers.

municipal-property.rationale: Inferred from the preference for state and civilisational unity; community ownership is not discussed and the state is the central actor.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Eurasianism favours a centralised empire or union, so joint bodies that merely coordinate would be too weak.

family-wage.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's emphasis on traditional family and social order.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Anachronistic or not addressed; no basis to infer a position.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's traditionalism and hostility to transhumanist and Western technological ideals.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Inferred from the strong state and its claim to oversight of society; payments are not discussed.

online-anonymity.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's strong state and anti-liberal stance; online identity is not discussed.

person-over-state.rationale: Eurasianists reject Western individualism in favour of the conciliar personality, in which the person is part of a church and national whole.

spiritual-nature.rationale: Orthodoxy and spiritual tradition are central to classical Eurasianism, and Dugin's traditionalism is explicitly anti-materialist.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Inferred from the preference for a unitary, strong state over federal limits on central authority.

gm-crops.rationale: Anachronistic for the classical school; neo-Eurasianist views on genetic engineering are not covered in the sources.

dense-cities.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; no basis for a stance.

racial-group-interests.rationale: Eurasianism defines the community by a supra-ethnic civilisation and Slavic-Turkic symbiosis rather than by race.

racial-pride.rationale: Inferred from the supra-ethnic, civilisational basis of identity; pride is placed in culture and civilisation, not race.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Eurasianism is built on empire and geopolitical expansion against the Atlantic bloc, so limiting force to defence is rejected.

language-defines-nation.rationale: Eurasianism treats Slavic and Turkic peoples as one civilisation despite differing languages, so shared language is not what defines a nation.

communal-electorates.rationale: Inferred: the Eurasianist state is a unitary, ideocratic order bound by shared civilisation, not communal electorates.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: Dugin's geopolitics casts the Atlantic bloc as an enemy working to weaken and break up Russia and Eurasia.

free-public-college.rationale: Not addressed; Eurasianists would accept state provision but the sources give no position on tuition.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Inferred: Eurasianists reject Western liberal market devices and favour state direction over price instruments; not discussed.

future-generations.rationale: Inferred from traditionalism and the idea of a civilisation continuing across generations; not discussed directly.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Dugin's traditionalism stresses family and religion with conventional gender roles, so extra weight for women's values is unlikely.

arms-reduction.rationale: Eurasianism is built on geopolitical rivalry and empire, so it favours strong forces rather than minimal arms.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Inferred from geopolitical realism and the strong-state outlook that prizes confidential negotiation.

capital-controls.rationale: Inferred from the strong-state, anti-liberal outlook and sovereignty against Atlanticism.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: Inferred from the ideology's call for a strong, centralised Eurasian state; no source discusses private armed groups.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Eurasianism is an ideology of empire and geopolitical struggle with the Atlantic bloc, so a duty to refuse state wars runs against it.

collective-bargaining.rationale: Inferred from the organic, corporatist-leaning state the classical Eurasianists favoured; sources do not address bargaining directly.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: The ideology never addressed income top-ups and adherents could read them either as statist support or as liberal welfare technique.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Inferred from its emphasis on state sovereignty and state direction of the economy over external or legal constraints.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Trubetskoy attacks Western domination of other peoples and neo-Eurasianism demands a multipolar order against Atlanticism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: Eurasianism wants a strong, authoritative state, not its dismantling.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: Classical Eurasianists envisioned an ideocratic state guided by one governing idea, though economic views were loose; inferred.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Inferred from its traditionalist, anti-materialist critique of Western modernity; no source discusses pricing nature.

sacred-nation.rationale: The people and civilisation, bound with Orthodoxy, are treated as an enduring spiritual unity, though the focus is civilisation rather than nation.

student-debt-relief.rationale: No source addresses student loans and the ideology is indifferent to the question.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Eurasianism presents Russia and its neighbours as a symbiotic whole and Russia as no coloniser; inferred from this.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Trubetskoy rejects universal human civilisation and the universalism of Western rights, holding that cultures are distinct.

public-service-media.rationale: Inferred from its preference for a strong state shaping culture and information, rather than independent public media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Eurasianists give Orthodoxy a leading, culture-defining role and treat civilisations as distinct, so they reject the idea that all religions are one truth.

farm-price-support.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strong, state-directed third-way economy and traditionalist protection of rural life.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: The strategic doctrine of an independent Eurasian great power opposed to the West treats Russia's nuclear arsenal as the basis of sovereignty.

workers-own-party.rationale: Inferred: Eurasianism calls for a single ideocratic, national leadership rather than class-based parties.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition is socially conservative and rejects Western universal human rights, but does not defend the practice, so it is split.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Not addressed; Dugin's traditionalism stresses traditional gender roles but Russian law already grants equal rights, so this is inferred as split.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Not addressed as a doctrine; Eurasianists stress the unity of Eurasian peoples around Russian, but a linguistic classification is not a core claim.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Inferred: a strong-state, anti-liberal ideology prefers state authority to private-law remedies.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Not addressed; classical Eurasianists favoured an ideocratic hierarchy and respect for native traditions in the empire, but no formal chiefs role.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not addressed; the tradition subordinates individual liberty to the collective, but its priorities are geopolitical and cultural, not environmental.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Inferred from the authoritarian, strong-state orientation favouring firm central control over judicial discretion.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Inferred from the emphasis on a unifying Russian-centred civilisation and rejection of Western multiculturalism.

no-compulsory-union.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strong, state-directed, corporatist character of neo-Eurasian economics.

voter-id.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the emphasis on a strong sovereign state and its control over who counts as the people.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: Classical Eurasianists gave Orthodoxy a leading role in the state, and neo-Eurasianism favours traditional religions, so legal equality of interpretations is not accepted.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: Eurasianists reject Western liberal democracy as a universal model and prefer an ideocratic or organic, participatory state to a procedural definition.

premarital-sex.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism is traditionalist and attacks Western sexual liberalism, so it does not endorse sex outside marriage.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Inferred from the stress on state sovereignty and order against Western information influence.

negative-income-tax.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the preference for a state-directed, socially protective economy over market-style cash schemes.

women-suffrage.rationale: Not addressed directly; classical Eurasianists distrusted parliamentary politics while neo-Eurasianists defend traditional gender roles, so adherents are split.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Religion, especially Orthodoxy, is treated as a foundation of civilisation, so the claim that it oppresses women is rejected.

race-social-construct.rationale: Trubetskoy rejects racial hierarchy but Eurasianism treats ethnic and civilisational identities as real and deep, so adherents are split.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Inferred from traditionalist opposition to Western gender-equality agendas.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Inferred from the collectivist, state-directed third-way economy; first-claim private ownership was not addressed.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: Eurasianists reject Western universalism and liberal international order, and Dugin treats Atlanticist institutions as instruments of the West.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Eurasianists stress Orthodoxy as cultural foundation but do not teach literal inerrancy; this is inferred and split.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist, anti-liberal outlook and the lack of any stated policy on gender guarantees in autonomy.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Eurasianists defended a strong state, but classical Eurasianists sought an ideocracy and not Marxist planning; this is inferred as split.

indirect-election.rationale: Classical Eurasianists proposed a selected ruling elite and rejected Western parliamentary democracy, so indirect selection is inferred as favoured.

national-church-status.rationale: Eurasianists gave Orthodoxy a central role in the state and national identity, as the RUDN article documents.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Eurasianism envisioned a Slavic-Turkic symbiosis of peoples within one state, which suggests some recognition of regions, though under a strong centre.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Eurasianism seeks imperial unity and Dugin's geopolitics treats borders as strategic, so a local vote deciding allegiance is inferred as disfavoured.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Inferred from the aim to reunite the former imperial space and reject borders imposed by outside powers.

simple-living.rationale: Not addressed; traditionalism points toward modest living but Eurasianists did not advocate self-sufficiency, so this is inferred as split.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Inferred from the imperial, unifying outlook that favours movement and integration across Eurasia; the question was never addressed.

equal-conscription.rationale: Inferred from the traditionalist outlook that assigns the military role to men; the question was not addressed directly.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: Eurasianism ties the civilisation to a specific continental homeland whose unity it defends, and ties Orthodoxy to that land and state.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the strong authoritarian state, which sits uneasily with the explicit arbitrary killing of suspects.

close-ties-china.rationale: Not addressed directly; Eurasianists want an anti-Atlantic bloc, but Dugin-style geopolitics treats China as a partner and a potential rival, so adherents are split.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism treats the Russian and Slavic-Turkic world as one civilisational space and backs Russia's role in the lands around it, though no specific funding policy is stated.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the collectivist, state-centred view of land and resources as the common patrimony of the Eurasian peoples.

self-ownership.rationale: Eurasianism rejects Western liberal individualism and puts the organic, conciliar community above the individual.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Not addressed; Eurasianism has no stated view on consumption taxes.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: Not addressed; the state is strong and paternal but targeting versus universal benefits is not discussed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: Inferred from the ideocratic leader-and-ruling-stratum model and Dugin's populist leadership, which downplay Western-style parties.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a state-directed economy that favours strategically important firms.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Inferred from the Eurasianist view that religions, Orthodoxy and Islam among them, are pillars of the state, which makes religion a basis of public life.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: Neo-Eurasianism and Dugin's traditionalism call for combining modern state power and technology with a revived archaic tradition, though the writers differ on how.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the traditional-family and religion-centred stance of Dugin and the Orthodox-inflected classical school.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from the anti-Western, strong-state, geopolitical stance that keeps strategic wealth under Eurasian control.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Eurasianism's rejection of Western liberal individualism and its collective, state-centred ideocracy; distributive justice is not discussed.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from hostility to Western-dominated global finance and support for a strong state; no source mentions such a tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Inferred: Eurasianists dismiss Western universalist framings but the sources never address racial disadvantage, so the answer is neutral.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Inferred from the strong-state, ideocratic model in which the state embodies the nation's mission and law is not subordinate to individual conscience.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from traditionalism and the emphasis on rootedness and national economy over technological progress; automation is not discussed.

multipolar-world.rationale: Eurasianism is built on opposing a unipolar Atlantic order: Trubetskoy argues for the equality of cultures against Romano-Germanic universalism, and Dugin's geopolitics sets Eurasia against the Atlantic bloc.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from rejection of materialist and Marxist frameworks in favour of civilisational and spiritual ones; value theory is not discussed.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred: strong national and civilisational loyalty is central, and some neo-Eurasianists add social-economic aims, but solidarity with workers abroad is not a theme.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: Eurasianism puts civilisational identity first yet is not a left project, so the framing of what the left should do does not map onto it.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from Eurasianism's rejection of Western liberal capitalism and of communist materialism alike; the combination is not discussed.

missingStatements.text: Ideas such as democracy and human rights are the product of one civilization, not universal values.
missingStatements.rationale: Trubetskoy called European universalism Romano-Germanic chauvinism and Dugin treats democracy and human rights as Western rather than universal.

missingStatements.text: No culture or civilization is higher or lower than another; they are only different.
missingStatements.rationale: Trubetskoy rejects the evolutionary ladder of cultures and says there is only similar and dissimilar.

missingStatements.text: The world should be divided among several great civilizational blocs rather than led by one superpower.
missingStatements.rationale: Eurasianism is built on opposition to US-led Atlanticism and the creation of a Eurasian bloc.

notes: Classical Eurasianism split into anti-Soviet and pro-Soviet currents and rejected ethnic nationalism and racial doctrines, while Dugin's version is described by critics as fascist and gives Russians priority. Economic answers are mostly inferred because the classical writers left economics undeveloped.
